comparison: Both strongly support the technical achievement and comprehensiveness of the EMG dataset. OpenEval R2 focuses on technical specifications (C26, C63-C70), while Peer R1 emphasizes the overall dataset quality (C3-C7, C26-C27, C65-C77, C86, C95-C96). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED with high confidence.

Both support claims about extensive motor unit identification (C3, C4, C6, C27). OpenEval R4 provides detailed quantitative validation, while Peer R1 praises this as part of the broader technical achievement. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both support the motor unit tracking methodology (C5, C7, C74-C77). OpenEval R5 notes moderate success rates and quality control measures, while Peer R1 includes tracking as part of the comprehensive technical achievement. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both support validation approaches (C71-C73). OpenEval R3 details the two complementary validation methods, while Peer R1 acknowledges rigorous validation as part of the overall technical rigor. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both support claims about dataset novelty and comprehensiveness (C86, C95, C96). OpenEval R20 validates specific quantitative claims, while Peer R1 praises the comprehensive assessment. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both strongly support the two-stage rate coding finding (C8, C88-C90). OpenEval R7 emphasizes statistical support and consistency with animal literature, while Peer R2 explicitly confirms this as a key contribution validating animal studies in humans. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both support differential initial acceleration findings (C9, C10, C82). OpenEval R8 provides detailed statistical validation, while Peer R2 acknowledges this as part of the two-stage pattern confirmation. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both address mechanistic interpretations of rate coding (C28, C29). OpenEval R11 rates as UNCERTAIN due to speculative nature, while Peer R2 accepts the interpretation as confirming animal studies. Divergence in confidence level despite addressing same claims.

Both support muscle-specific differences in rate coding (C11, C12). OpenEval R9 emphasizes statistical significance and generality, while Peer R3 confirms the finding as part of the two-stage pattern. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both address the linear increase phase interpretation (C32, C33). OpenEval R12 rates as UNCERTAIN due to mechanistic speculation, while Peer R3 accepts the finding as valid. Divergence in evaluation type despite similar claim coverage.

Both address hysteresis findings (C13, C14, C91, C92). OpenEval R10 supports with statistical evidence but notes variability, while Peer R4 rates as UNCERTAIN due to methodological concerns about using torque for hysteresis quantification. Significant divergence in confidence.

Both address mechanistic interpretations of hysteresis (C40-C43). OpenEval R14 rates as UNCERTAIN due to speculative nature, while Peer R4 rates as UNCERTAIN due to methodological limitations. Both uncertain but for different reasons.

Both support the gain control framework and challenge to onion skin principle (C34-C37, C93, C97). OpenEval R13 emphasizes data support for the conceptual framework, while Peer R5 strongly endorses the interpretation but notes prior work (Monster and Chan 1977) reduces novelty claims. Both SUPPORTED with caveats.

Both address the functional framework synthesis (C94). OpenEval R21 supports the interpretation while noting it's inferential, while Peer R5 includes this as part of the broader gain control framework. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Perfect claim overlap (C44-C48) on muscle-specific mechanistic interpretations. OpenEval R15 rates as UNCERTAIN due to speculative nature and lack of direct human evidence, while Peer R6 rates as SUPPORTED, accepting the speculation as reasonable. Significant divergence in evaluation type.

Perfect claim overlap (C49-C56) on functional interpretations. OpenEval R16 rates as UNCERTAIN due to inferential nature requiring validation, while Peer R7 rates as SUPPORTED, accepting functional interpretations as reasonable extensions. Significant divergence in evaluation type.

Both address extrapolations to different conditions (C38, C39, C15). OpenEval R18 rates as UNCERTAIN requiring experimental validation, while Peer R9 rates as SUPPORTED with contextual acceptance. Divergence in confidence level.

Both address experimental methods and ethical procedures (C1, C2, C57-C62). OpenEval R1 emphasizes rigorous design and ethical oversight, while Peer R8 praises methodological rigor but notes small sample size and questions muscle selection justification. Both SUPPORTED with Peer noting limitations.

Both address experimental design and analytical framework (C23-C25, C78-C81, C83). OpenEval R6 rates as UNCERTAIN due to unverified assumptions about linear force and synaptic inputs, while Peer R8 rates as SUPPORTED praising rigorous methods. Significant divergence in evaluation type.

Both address statistical methods (C84, C85). OpenEval R19 supports the hierarchical modeling approach, while Peer R8 includes statistical rigor as part of overall methodological praise. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.
OpenEval R17 evaluates background literature and scientific context (C16-C22) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.
